Better approach: Use apply_template tool with molecule_smiles = ??? and template_id = 2895. Need target SMILES. Likely the product is the first SMILES: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". That's a complex heterocycle. The second SMILES is "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F" which is a sulfonyl chloride. Maybe the target molecule is a sulfonamide formed from those two? Actually the product of reacting those would be a sulfonamide linking the amine to sulfonyl chloride. The template 2895 appears to be a sulfonamide formation? Let's inspect mapped_rxn: It shows product on left? The reaction arrow: left side is reactants? It shows a nitro aromatic (O=[N+](O-)[c...]) attached to a heterocycle? Right side is product: a tertiary amine with a phenyl nitro? Actually the product SMILES on right side corresponds to the first SMILES? Let's decode: Right side: [CH3][C]([CH3])([CH3])O C(=O) N1CH2CH2N(...). That matches the first SMILES: tert-butyl ester? Actually first SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1. That is a tert-butyl carbamate? Wait O=C(O)C? Actually CC(C)(C)O C(=O) N1... That's a tert-butoxy carbonyl (Boc) attached to N1. So product is a Boc-protected amine attached to heterocycle. The left side includes nitro aromatic? Hmm.

Thus template 2895 likely is a Boc protection of an amine? Actually left side includes O=[N+](O-)[c...] which is nitro group on aromatic, not Boc. The right side includes Boc group. So the transformation is conversion of a nitro aromatic? Not sure.

Nevertheless, we can just apply the template using tool apply_template with molecule_smiles = the product SMILES (first one) and template_id = "2895". Let's do that.
